hypothesis: The unchanged SPCX cash-open gap-reversal mechanism may transfer to MU because both are cash-session equity references, while MU supplies an independent asset and deeper opportunity set.

portfolio_contract.sizing_reason: largest tested notional with 100-percent two-sided visible-depth completion across the exact MU archive sample

stress_contract.historical_fee_limitation: current resolved account fee inputs are modeled across the archive because historical account fee-state changes are unavailable

fee_evidence.scope_note: The rate is an account-level HIP-3 fee input; the MU liquidity artifact independently freezes the identical fee formula and values.

advance_requirements.development: positive nominal and stress net, PF above one, positive stress net after largest-winner removal, both directions observed, at least two positive stress folds, no liquidation, and technically resolved selected lifecycles
advance_requirements.validation: only the frozen development identity may enter validation; no replacement or retuning
advance_requirements.holdout: only a validation-advanced frozen identity may enter untouched holdout
advance_requirements.portfolio: a live proposal additionally requires source parity, route-exit parity, shared-account interaction replay, and explicit human approval

known_failure_modes: SPCX development may be an asset-specific or window-specific result rather than a transferable session effect.
MU p99 visible execution cost is large relative to the 80-bps protective stop.
Historical mark cadence gaps may make selected lifecycles technically unresolved.
The current account fee state is modeled historically and may differ from archived fee state.
Development success would still be selection evidence rather than untouched confirmation.
falsifier: Reject the unchanged transfer if development fails the frozen economic or technical checks; do not rescue it by tuning thresholds, selecting a side, changing size after PnL, or opening validation for a replacement identity.
